title: The Confidential Client Report
subject: Handling a Confidential Client Report
scenario: You are working on a client project and receive a report containing customer names, contact details, project costs and confidential business information. A colleague from another department asks you to upload the report to a shared folder accessible to several employees across the organization.
email_note: TASK: What is the most appropriate way to handle this confidential information?
options: Upload the report because all employees within the organization are authorized to access internal business information.
Check the information classification and the colleague's business need, then share it only through an approved, access-controlled company platform.
Remove the client name from the document and upload the remaining information to the shared folder without further approval.
Send the report through a personal email account so the colleague can access it without requesting company-folder permissions.
explanation: Confidential information should only be shared with authorized individuals who have a legitimate business need. Use approved storage and access controls.

title: The Unattended Workstation
subject: Workstation Security Awareness
scenario: You are working on a confidential project report at your desk. You need to leave your workstation for a 15-minute meeting. Your computer is unlocked, printed client documents are on your desk and your access card is beside the keyboard. Other employees and visitors are moving through the office.
email_note: TASK: Which action best follows corporate workplace security practices?
options: Leave the workstation open because the meeting is short and the office is accessible only to employees.
Close the report but leave the computer unlocked so another team member can continue the work if required.
Lock the workstation, secure confidential documents in an appropriate location and keep the access card with you.
Ask a nearby colleague to watch the desk while leaving the documents and computer accessible.
explanation: Lock your workstation whenever you leave it unattended, secure sensitive documents and never leave access credentials or cards exposed.
evidence_caption: Corporate clean desk and workstation security scenario.

title: Spot the Mistakes in This Email
subject: URGENT: Unusual Login – Verify Within 10 Minutes
scenario:
From: Microsoft 365 Security
Reply-To: security-verify@outlook-account-check.example

Dear Valued User,

We detected a suspicious login from an unknown location. Your mailbox will be deleted in 10 minutes unless you confirm your password and MFA code using the link below.

Click here: https://microsoft365.com/security
Actual destination: https://microsoft365-security-check.example/verify

Please do not contact your IT department during this automated security procedure.

Regards,
Microsoft Account Protection
email_note: TASK: Identify the combination of mistakes that makes this email suspicious.
options: The email is suspicious only because it does not include the employee's full name; the remaining details are normal for an automated security alert.
The email is suspicious because Microsoft security alerts never mention unusual sign-ins or ask users to review account activity.
The email contains a mismatched sender and reply-to domain, an unrelated destination, an extreme deadline, a request for an MFA code and an instruction to avoid IT.
The email is safe because the displayed link contains microsoft365.com and the message provides a recognizable security explanation.
explanation: Multiple indicators appear together: a non-Microsoft sender, mismatched reply-to, misleading link, urgency, request for an MFA code and discouragement from contacting IT.
evidence_caption: Fictional phishing email created for awareness training.

title: The HR Benefits Announcement
subject: Which Benefits Enrollment Email Is Genuine?
scenario:
EMAIL A
From: hr@fujisilvertech.com
Subject: Annual Benefits Enrollment
Message: The annual benefits review is open. Employees can access the information through the established HR portal. No password or payment information is requested by email.

EMAIL B
From: hr-benefits@fujisilvertech-careers.example
Subject: Benefits Enrollment – Immediate Action
Message: Submit your employee ID, password and bank account information through the attached form to retain your benefits.

TASK: Which email should employees rely on?
email_note: A familiar HR subject does not prove that a message is genuine. Check the sender and requested information.
options: Email B, because benefits enrollment requires employees to provide complete identity and banking details before a deadline.
Both emails, because benefits teams may use different external platforms for employee information.
Email B, if the attachment uses the company's logo and contains the correct employee identification format.
Email A, because it uses the company domain and directs employees to the established HR portal rather than requesting passwords or banking details by email.
explanation: Email A follows a safer communication pattern. Email B uses an unrelated domain and requests highly sensitive information through an attachment.

title: The Hidden Reply-To Address
subject: Urgent Supplier Confirmation
scenario:
From: procurement@fujisilvertech.com
Reply-To: procurement.confirmation@external-mail.example

Hello Team,

Please confirm the attached supplier quotation before the purchase order is released. Reply to this email with the approved supplier's bank details and contact information.

The message appears to originate from an internal procurement address, but replies will be directed to a different external address.
email_note: TASK: What is the most important technical detail to investigate before responding?
options: The Reply-To address differs from the visible sender and redirects responses to an external domain; verify the request through a known internal contact.
The email has no visible attachment size, which proves that the sender's mailbox has been compromised.
The sender uses a company domain, so the request can be accepted if the quotation contains a valid supplier reference.
The message should be treated as genuine because external reply addresses are commonly used by procurement departments.
explanation: A different Reply-To address can redirect sensitive replies to an attacker even when the visible sender looks legitimate. Verify independently before sharing supplier or financial information.

title: The Supplier Gift Offer
subject: Supplier Relationship and Gift Policy
scenario: You are part of a team evaluating proposals from three suppliers. One supplier privately offers you an expensive smartphone as a thank-you gift before the final selection. They mention that accepting it will help maintain a strong business relationship. You are involved in reviewing the supplier's proposal.
email_note: TASK: What is the most ethical and professionally appropriate response?
options: Accept the gift because it is offered personally and does not directly change the supplier's quoted price.
Accept the gift but disclose it to your manager after the supplier selection process is completed.
Decline the gift, disclose the offer through the appropriate company channel and follow the conflict-of-interest policy.
Accept the gift if the supplier provides it to the entire procurement team rather than to one employee.
explanation: An expensive gift offered during a supplier evaluation can create an actual or perceived conflict of interest. Decline it and disclose the offer according to company policy.
evidence_caption: Corporate ethics and supplier relationship scenario.

title: The Supplier Bank Change
subject: Revised Bank Details – Invoice NS-1182
scenario: A regular supplier sends an email from its familiar address. It requests a change to its beneficiary bank account and attaches a bank confirmation letter. The message states that all future payments must go to the new account immediately. The purchase order and invoice amounts match existing records.
email_note: TASK: Which control should be completed before changing the beneficiary details?
options: Update the beneficiary because the sender address and invoice amount match the supplier's existing records.
Accept the attached bank letter after checking its logo, formatting and account-holder name.
Call a phone number included in the new email and ask the person to confirm the bank account.
Verify the change using a previously registered supplier contact, then obtain the required independent approval and retain the verification record.
explanation: A familiar email account may be compromised. Use previously verified contact information, not details supplied in the change request, and follow the payment approval process.

title: The QR Code Login Trap
subject: Scan to Restore Your Microsoft 365 Access
scenario:
Dear Employee,

Your Microsoft 365 session is scheduled for termination. Scan the attached QR code to restore access. The QR code will open a secure authentication page. If asked, enter your password and approve the MFA notification to complete the process.

This procedure must be completed before the end of the day.
email_note: TASK: What is the safest response to this unexpected QR-code authentication request?
options: Scan the code using a personal phone instead of a company device to reduce the risk to the corporate network.
Scan the code but stop before entering the password; the QR image itself cannot expose company credentials.
Do not scan it or approve unexpected MFA prompts; verify the alleged access problem through the established IT support channel.
Forward the QR code to a colleague and ask them to test whether the authentication page looks genuine.
explanation: QR codes can conceal phishing destinations. Never enter credentials or approve unexpected MFA prompts based on an unsolicited message.
evidence_caption: Fictional QR phishing simulation. No active QR destination is included.

title: The Duplicate Payment Request
subject: Urgent: Supplier Claims Invoice Is Still Unpaid
scenario: A message from Finance asks the accounts team to pay invoice INV-2481 a second time. The supplier claims that the first payment was not received. The email says reconciliation can be completed next week because the delivery is urgent. The original payment status has not yet been confirmed.
email_note: TASK: Which action best prevents duplicate payment fraud?
options: Hold the second payment, trace the original transaction through bank and ledger records, and confirm the supplier's claim through an established contact.
Release the payment if the invoice number and amount match the purchase order, then reconcile both payments later.
Ask the supplier to resend the invoice with a new date and process it as a separate transaction.
Make a partial payment now and release the balance once the supplier confirms receipt.
explanation: A matching invoice does not prove that payment is outstanding. Reconcile the original transaction and independently confirm the supplier's claim before paying again.

title: The Executive Impersonation Test
subject: Confidential – Process This Payment Immediately
scenario:
Hello,

I am in a confidential meeting and cannot speak on the phone. Please arrange an urgent payment to the account in the attached document. This is a management-approved activity. Do not inform the finance manager until the transaction is complete. I will explain everything later.

Regards,
Managing Director
email_note: TASK: Which combination of indicators most strongly suggests executive impersonation?
options: The email uses a senior job title and refers to a confidential meeting, which are both normal business practices.
The request uses an executive-looking sender domain, demands an urgent payment, bypasses Finance and insists on secrecy without independent approval.
The message does not include a formal signature block, which is the only reliable indicator of impersonation.
The attachment is a PDF rather than a spreadsheet, so the request should be accepted after antivirus scanning.
explanation: Executive impersonation commonly combines a lookalike sender domain, urgency, secrecy and pressure to bypass normal payment controls. Verify through a known executive contact and the established finance process.
